statement: A store rents paddleboards. The total cost $C(h)$, in dollars, of renting one paddleboard for $h$ hours is a linear function of $h$. Some values are shown in the table. $$\begin{array}{c|c} h & C(h) \\ \hline 2 & 38 \\ 5 & 65 \\ 9 & 101 \end{array}$$ The cost includes a fixed fee that is charged no matter how long the rental lasts. What is the fixed fee, in dollars?

choices.misconception: I found that the cost goes up by 9 dollars per hour and gave the 9 as the fixed fee, but 9 is the hourly rate.
I saw the cost rise by 27 dollars from one row to the next and stepped back one row from 38 to get $38 - 27 = 11$, but going from 2 hours to 0 hours is only 2 hours, not 3.
I subtracted the number of hours from the cost, $38 - 2 = 36$, instead of subtracting 2 hours times the hourly rate.

hints: The fixed fee is the cost when $h = 0$.
Use two rows of the table to find how much the cost rises for each extra hour.
From $h = 2$ to $h = 5$ the cost rises by $27$ dollars in $3$ hours, so $9$ dollars per hour. Remove $2$ hours of that from $38$.

solutions.reliable: The slope is $\dfrac{65 - 38}{5 - 2} = \dfrac{27}{3} = 9$ dollars per hour. Check with the last row: $\dfrac{101 - 65}{9 - 5} = 9$. So $C(h) = 9h + b$, and $38 = 9(2) + b$ gives $b = 20$. The fixed fee is $C(0) = 20$ dollars.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
